replacement_or_supplementary_sources.what_it_supports: Full-year 2024 US+Canada: 3,625 incidents (+27% YoY), $454.9M losses, avg $202,364/incident. Q1 2024 +46% YoY, Q2 +33%.
Independently corroborates CargoNet figures: 3,625 incidents (+27%), $454.9M total losses (up from $331.9M 2023).
NICB 2024: 2,217 US cargo thefts; +27% YoY. California + Texas >50% of incidents. No H1-specific 49% figure published.
Corroborates rising NA theft trend and tactic evolution (facility thefts up, +48% insider participation in NA). Does not publish 49% H1 or $115,230 avg loss.

revised_claim_text: Cargo theft in the US and Canada reached record levels in 2024: Verisk CargoNet recorded 3,625 incidents (+27% YoY) and $454.9M in estimated losses (up from $331.9M in 2023); average loss per incident $202,364. NICB independently confirmed the 27% full-year rise. Q1 2024 saw the sharpest spike (+46% YoY); Q2 moderated to +33%. [The Overhaul-reported '49% H1 2024 rise' and '$115,230 average loss' originate from a single vendor press release and are not corroborated by CargoNet, NICB, or BSI/TT Club — should not be cited as independent statistics. The 'Overhaul: 2,500 Incident Response Operations, $35M recovered' figure is vendor self-reported with zero independent corroboration — remove or label [VENDOR-SELF-REPORTED].]
footnote_for_artifact: Cargo theft 2024 statistics: Verisk CargoNet 2024 Annual Report (cargonet.com/news-and-events/cargonet-in-the-media/2024-theft-trends); NICB 2024 Annual Cargo Theft Report (nicb.org); BSI/TT Club 2024 Cargo Theft Report (bsigroup.com). Overhaul vendor figures retained only with explicit attribution caveat.
notes: Three Tier-1 independent trackers (CargoNet, NICB, BSI/TT Club) corroborate +27% YoY in 2024 across the full year. Overhaul's 49% H1 figure is directionally consistent with CargoNet's Q1 +46%, but is a different unit (H1 vs Q1) and reflects Overhaul's own customer base (biased sample). Drop the vendor-specific %, retain CargoNet/NICB primary. Upgrade Low → Medium because corroborated independent data now anchors the trend even though specific Overhaul figures stay vendor-only.
